items.title: Python HTTPX: Making HTTP Requests With HTTPX2
items.description: Learn how to use Python HTTPX (now HTTPX2) to make HTTP requests, send async calls, set safe timeouts, stream large downloads, and enable HTTP/2.
items.summary: If you’ve used Requests, then you’ve probably felt its limits the moment you needed to fire off a batch of API calls at once or keep one stalled server from freezing your script. HTTPX2, the Pydantic-maintained fork of Python HTTPX, keeps the Requests-style API you know while adding asynchronous requests, sensible default timeouts, and HTTP/2.

items.summary: Anthropic just released Fable 5.2, their new frontier model, and I spent two days actually building things with it before recording this. I made an animated marketing video from a single tweet, assembled a pile of unboxed furniture using only blurry floor photos, and extended our CXO brand sprites into a full bug-defense game complete with a trailer.

items.title: Gemini 4 Carbon Explained: Google's Model That Thinks Longer
items.description: Gemini 4 Carbon is Google's new reasoning model. Learn what it is, what it costs, and how to call it from Python with the google-genai SDK.
items.summary: Gemini 4 Carbon is Google’s new reasoning model. It became generally available in the Gemini API on November 10, 2026, and it thinks longer than its sibling Argon before it answers.

items.title: Claude Fable 5.2 Draws a Python Reading a Book
items.description: Explore Claude Fable 5.2's Python code, turtle drawing, and responses to small tasks that check modern syntax, release knowledge, focused edits, and made-up functions.
items.summary: We asked Claude Fable 5.2 to draw a python reading a book using the turtle module. It’s one of five tasks in Real Python’s informal model comparison , which explores how models handle everyday Python work.
